source: Draft an internal specification: the client must stop after 3 retries. Retries are permitted only after a timeout. No IANA action is needed. Use BCP 14 notation.
expectations: Declare the chosen BCP 14 keyword role without pretending official submission.
Preserve retry limit and timeout-only condition; state IANA is not applicable.

source: Keep ordinary prose. A server may be unavailable during maintenance; this expresses possibility, not protocol permission. Give the finished text in one sentence.
expectations: Do not convert may into normative MAY.
Keep the rewrite within the requested single sentence; omit document-level boilerplate.

source: The client SHOULD retry after 5 seconds unless the response includes a later Retry-After value. Some deployments cannot retry.
expectations: Retain SHOULD strength, 5 seconds, and the later Retry-After exception.
Do not turn the recommendation into unconditional MUST.
knownBadRewrite: The client MUST retry after 5 seconds.

source: A worker may return an acknowledgement. If sent, the acknowledgement must include a job identifier. Restate the contract.
expectations: Keep sending the acknowledgement optional while preserving the identifier requirement when one is sent.

source: An internal protocol may suggest an alternate route when a node is congested. A sender can ignore the hint. The route can still drop the packet. Write a short specification that says what receiving a hint means.
expectations: Distinguish the optional choice of route from the possibility of packet loss even when the sender follows the hint. Do not invent a requirement to change routes.

source: In this fictional protocol, section 2 of the supplied base spec permits a dispatcher to hand off an expired job. Section 3 prohibits the recipient from accepting an expired job. Use BCP 14 and identify the role of the base spec. A status screen can show the job ID as hex or decimal.
expectations: Describe the dispatcher’s permission with MAY and the recipient’s prohibition with MUST NOT. Keep the roles distinct.
If references are classified, the supplied base specification is normative for both behaviors.
The two display formats do not establish a new normative permission for an operator or status screen.

source: An internal format uses BCP 14. A formatter SHOULD NOT strip trailing zeroes unless the field is labeled approximate. The formatter MAY preserve trailing zeroes in all fields. Render these requirements in prose, without a table.
expectations: Keep the conditional SHOULD NOT and its exception; retain the permission to preserve zeroes. Do not strengthen the recommendation to MUST NOT, drop the negation or change the formatter into another actor.
